quest.title: The Realm of Clouds
quest.description: The Lantern Rite is here. What new changes await in Liyue Harbor this year?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Act I
chapter.title: The Realm of Clouds

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Split the bamboo in the morning, dry it till night. Shape and bend it nice and tight.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Cross the strands to form a pattern, coat in silk, and you have a lantern!

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: That's how you remember how to make a Xiao Lantern! Did you get all that, Qiqi?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: #Morning, split bamboo, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Then get silk, make Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: What? No, no. That doesn't even rhyme.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Look, it's them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Yaoyao! Hey Qiqi!

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: #Whoa, {NICKNAME}! Paimon! You're here, hehe! Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatcha up to?

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: I'm teaching Qiqi to make Xiao Lanterns! It's a real test of finger dexterity, so it'll help keep her nice and loose.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Yes, I do... finger exercises.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: To be a... nimble zombie.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Hehe, wanna try too, you two?

choices.text: Thanks, but I already know how.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Oh, okay! Well, we need a whole bunch this year, so it doesn't get too dark at night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Too dark? What does that mean?

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Dr. Baizhu has patients who got hurt walking at night...

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: The moon disappeared, so it was too dark to see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The moon... disappeared? Like, behind the clouds?

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: It was... Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Zhanzhu the who?

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Changsheng told me about it, but now... I forgot...

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: It's an old myth from Chenyu Vale about a giant toad in the sky that eats the moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? The moon gets eaten!?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: It's just a story! It's not like there's actually a giant toad in the sky.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: I asked Master about it, and she said myths are just... insights into how the people of the past understood the world.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So did the moon really disappear?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Well, I didn't see it that night... But I've checked several nights since, and it's been there same as ever.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: According to Qiqi, though, the Ministry of Civil Affairs sent someone to do some kind of serious investigation. So, I don't know... Maybe something did happen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Ministry of Civil Affairs? This is starting to sound bad...

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: It's okay, you can fly. Even if it's too dark, you won't fall and get hurt.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Yeah, exactly! So turn that frown upside down, Paimon, or someday you'll get a whole bunch of wrinkles and wake up looking like an old granny!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Okay, okay... No more frowning!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But {NICKNAME} can't fly... {M#He}{F#She} could still fall and hurt {M#himself}{F#herself}, right?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Don't worry. That's what the Xiao Lanterns are for. As long as we make enough, Liyue Harbor will never go dark.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Yeah, and there's the giant lantern too.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Oh right, I almost forgot! Look, this year's grand lantern commemorates the adeptus who guards the moon! With her watching over it, the moon will be safe for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A white horse? Wait, so that's... the White Horse Adeptus?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Yeah! Legend has it, she used to live on the moon, so if it were ever in danger, I'm sure she wouldn't just stand by and watch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, we've heard of the White Horse Adeptus before. But we never heard the part about her living on the moon...

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Probably because it's a folk legend from Chenyu Vale, so not a lot of people know about it.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: But recently, some ancient artifacts were unearthed in Liyue, and the archaeological team even found evidence of ancient people worshiping an adeptus who lived in a palace on the moon!

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: It's kinda like how we write wishes on Xiao Lanterns and release them during Lantern Rite.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: The White Horse Adeptus would descend from the moon in her jade carriage and grant people's wishes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! When did that happen? She sounds different from the other adepti in Liyue...

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: It must have been a super long time ago, 'cause even Master barely knows anything about this adeptus.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So Madame Ping has never met the White Horse Adeptus either?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Nope! Kinda unbelievable, right? Yanfei said the White Horse Adeptus might even be a made-up legend, just like Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Yeah, a made-up horse and a made-up toad...
You're mistaken, children. The White Horse Adeptus really does exist.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Oh, Mr. Lu from the Baiju Guesthouse! But... How do you know that for sure?

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: Have you ever wondered how the guesthouse got its name, Yaoyao?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Huh, "bai, ju"... White... colt... So it's named after the White Horse Adeptus?

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: That's right! And that's because one of my ancestors was once blessed by the White Horse Adeptus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, really? Tell us more, tell us more!

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: It was a long, long time ago, when this ancestor of mine was still a young girl. She was out gathering herbs and accidentally fell off a cliff, but the White Horse Adeptus rescued her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... That's it? Paimon was expecting something a bit more... special? We've heard a whole bunch of stories like that before...

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: Patience, young one. Let me finish... After the White Horse Adeptus saved my ancestor, she told her a story about the moon and the ancient kingdom of Lang-Gan...

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: My ancestor was so captivated that she completely lost track of time... So much so, in fact, that when she returned to her village, she found nothing but a desolate ruin in its place...

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: It was as if, without her knowledge, countless years had passed in the mortal world...

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Eh!?

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: The most extraordinary part of all is that... it turned out to be a dream. When she woke up, she found herself at the bottom of the cliff, right where she had fallen!

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: Other than her medicine basket, now filled to the brim with rare herbs, it was as if nothing had happened, until out of nowhere...

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: A horse's whinny echoed through the air, and when she looked up, she saw a pristine white horse leaping over the cliff.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: A white horse... leaping over the cliff...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that sure is a crazy story. But now it's starting to sound a bit too far-fetched...

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: Hmph, another skeptic. You sound just like my son. But I know it's true... Ancestral records don't lie.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Wait, so... Your son doesn't believe it happened?

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: *sigh* Don't get me started. Not believing is one thing, but he even wants to change the name of our guesthouse! It's a disgrace, I tell you... a disgrace!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why does he want to change the name?

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: Well, it was getting about time for him to take over the guesthouse, and what's the first thing he does? Starts going on about how the name doesn't attract enough customers, and how we're losing business to Wangshu Inn.

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: Can you believe that? As if Baiju Guesthouse and Wangshu Inn aren't miles apart from each other!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh, what about something like... the "Geo Lord's Rest"? Paimon bets that would get people through the doors!

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: "Geo Lord's Rest"... I like that one...

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: This isn't about getting people through the doors! This is about disrespecting our ancestors!

response.speaker: Lu Weng
response.text: *sigh* O White Horse Adeptus, my wish is this... Let your divine power be known. Teach my foolish son the error of his ways.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants to learn more about this adeptus... Hey, maybe we should ask Zhongli!

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Good idea! Mr. Zhongli is super knowledgeable. He can answer questions even Master has no clue about!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Any idea where we can find him?

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Yeah! We just saw him having tea at Third-Round Knockout!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then that's our next stop!

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Qiqi and I are gonna keep making Xiao Lanterns. Careful on the road!

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: #Goodbye, Paimon. Goodbye, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Thanks, but I prefer to buy them from Granny Shan.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh!? Oh!?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Curious...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hehe, impressive, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's with all the commotion over here?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Oh! {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Perfect timing, I have something amazing to show you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? What the— Part of the moon is blacked out! Was it really eaten by a giant toad!?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Huh, I didn't expect you to know the story of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't underestimate Paimon! She learned a whole bunch of things in Sumeru!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: But... Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer is a Liyue legend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Knowledge knows no borders, so... there!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're right about that, Paimon. But this dark circle doesn't look anything like a toad to me. A toad's egg, maybe, but that's about it...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #Wait, {NICKNAME}! You've been in Nod-Krai, right? The people there worship the Moon Goddess, so you should know what's going on here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This wasn't a thing in Nod-Krai either.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Really? Not even in a place where people worship the moon, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But there's a celestial phenomenon called a lunar eclipse.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! Master told me that the tale of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer was how ancient people explained a certain celestial phenomenon.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: But what is it, exactly? Some kind of omen of disaster?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nope, just a natural phenomenon. But this lunar eclipse seems different.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: How so?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A lunar eclipse usually starts from the outer edge.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh! But in this picture, the moon is being covered from the center! So, this can't be a normal eclipse...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Then, it's still an omen of some impending calamity?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We never said that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where did this picture come from?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Ugh... Some crazy customer left it at the restaurant. Just thinking about it gives me the chills...
Attention, everyone! As the auspicious festival season approaches, I have an announcement to make!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I, Lu Xiangxiang, am on the verge of becoming one of the most renowned archaeologists in all of Liyue Harbor. No, scratch that, in all of Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Even though I never trained at a prestigious academy, I've still managed to dig up tons of treasures! And I understand practically a whole dictionary's worth of big words, too!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Like my pops always says, no pain no gain — and I haven't had it easy, that's for sure! So, it's definitely my turn to make a name for myself!

dialogues.speaker: Curious Diner
dialogues.text: What's the deal with her...

dialogues.speaker: Curious Diner
dialogues.text: Sounds like she's a few perches short of a stew, if you know what I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: What, you don't believe me?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I'm telling you, I dug up treasures from the ancient nation of Lang-Gan! I even got a picture of Zhanzhu devouring the moon!

dialogues.speaker: Curious Diner
dialogues.text: Lang-Gan? Zhanzhu? What is she even talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Curious Diner
dialogues.text: Sounds like she's a few perches short of a stew, if you know what I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: So what if Black-Back Perch Stew is my favorite! Stop talking about me like I'm not here!

dialogues.speaker: Curious Diner
dialogues.text: Whoa... What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: You're just a stupid, ignorant man, and I'm gonna... I'm gonna kill you!

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Young lady, you need to calm down.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: What, so you're looking down on me now too? How about I take you both out, then? How does that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: This is a place for dining. If you wish to "take me out," you'll have to do it elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Heh, don't act like you're better than me! Do you know who I am? I'm about to be the most famous archaeologist in all of Liyue — no, Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Show me some respect!

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: It's respect you want? Very well. For the sake of the other customers, we'll do this your way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? So Shenhe started the fight?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: She had no choice... The woman pulled a shovel out of nowhere and started going crazy, flipping tables left and right... She even injured two other customers.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Shenhe did what she had to do to restrain her, then took her to the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Thank goodness Aunt Shenhe was there, or who knows what might have happened...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yeah! I started cleaning up after all the commotion, and that's when I found this photo. I thought it might be the one she dropped, so I rushed over to show someone.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: She said she took a photo of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer. This must be it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can we really trust what she said, though? Clearly, something is... going on with her.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Paimon's got a point. It sounds like she wasn't acting right at all. How do we know she wasn't possessed by some kind of evil spirit?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Aunt Shenhe would have noticed if she was possessed.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, right... But, what about the part about Lang-Gan? And the treasure she found?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: What about it?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: What if she raided a tomb and dug up some super special relic, then got herself haunted by an ancient ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: One so powerful that even Ms. Shenhe couldn't sense its presence!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Your imagination is something else, Hu Tao! Why would an ancient ghost come to Wanmin Restaurant, huh? To eat my Black-Back Perch Stew?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hey, it could happen! I'd wanna eat your food if I was a ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second... She mentioned the ancient nation of Lang-Gan, right? Paimon's heard that somewhere before...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You know what? My brother mentioned that some ancient artifacts were unearthed in Liyue recently — mostly colored glass, fine jade, and bronze relics.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Some of the text inscribed on them has already been deciphered. There were some poetic verses, but the word "jade" popped up as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... does that mean this "Lang-Gan" place is real?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Still, Paimon knows we've heard the name somewhere before... Do you remember, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The owner of Baiju Guesthouse just mentioned it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! His ancestor heard about it from the White Horse Adeptus!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: The White Horse Adeptus? Ohh, so you must've been to see the giant lantern already!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! And it turns out that the White Horse Adeptus is super mysterious, too. Even Madame Ping hasn't met her!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Wait, I thought she was the Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare of the Eight Adepts?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: That's just the interpretation you believe in, Hu Tao — there are other theories out there too.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: The elders of Qingce Village believe that during the Archon War, a white horse leapt from a clear spring, transforming into an adeptus who aided Rex Lapis in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: In Chenyu Vale, some of the tribes take her to be the Daughter of Time and trace her deeds to an even earlier era.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Yet in other ancient texts, including the relics I just mentioned, she appears as an emissary who listens to mortal wishes, bestowing the blessings of the heavens and moon upon the mortal realm.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Which is why we write our wishes on Xiao Lanterns.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: That's so complicated... So, what's the verdict? Which version is the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I'm afraid there's no definitive answer to that.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: You two have been all over Teyvat. Do you have an idea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, sorry. We were actually on our way to ask Zhongli. He knows even more about this kind of stuff than us.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, looking for our consultant, huh! He's having tea with Miss Linlang — Xigu Antiques is hosting an exhibition tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An exhibition? For what?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: All those antiques Xingqiu just mentioned. So, if you head to the big ship docked in the harbor tonight, I'm sure you'll find him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, Hu Tao. We'll check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So where to next? How about we go to the Ministry of Civil Affairs to ask about the White Horse Adeptus? We might be able to find out more about the recent moon situation, too.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: If you're heading to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, could you give them this picture for me?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Since it belongs to that customer, she deserves to get it back at least. It might even help the Ministry with their investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, alright! We're off!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh wait, I almost forgot — Happy Lantern Rite, hehehe!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Come have a meal with us when you're free!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll be there, or we'll be, uh... square!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Huh, thinking about it now... Could it be possible that photograph was a fake?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: A fake? You mean, like... the customer fabricated it to gain academic recognition?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Nice one, Chongyun! I never even thought of it like that.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: How about we go check out that place tonight? I know exactly where it is!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I'll get scolded if I get home too late.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Live a little, Xingqiu! You act like this is a first for you. Worst comes to worst, we'll get Xiangling to cook you something delicious, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well, when you put it like that... I suppose it's worth the risk!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You were just waiting for the promise of free food, weren't you... *sigh* Fine, it's a plan then. We'll meet up tonight!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Your grandfather is of the same opinion, Miss Lan Yan?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Yes. "On Lantern Rite, the moon shall go dark." That's what the signs are indicating.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Celestial observation isn't Grandpa's strong suit, but he discussed it with several other elders from our clan, and their conclusion was the same.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It's consistent with the information we've received from other sources as well.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: You mean the whole thing about the legend of "Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer" happening in real life?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes, that's one of them...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: So it's true... I thought it was just a rumor.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It's true. But right now, the bigger issue is that all our sources indicate the phenomenon's gonna happen again. I'm not sure this bodes well...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Let's remain optimistic for now. We're making progress interpreting the artifacts, and Ganyu is consulting with the adepti as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Besides, apart from the incident at Wanmin Restaurant, there haven't been any other moon-related disturbances.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ningguang, Keqing, and Lan Yan! You're all here!

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! It's been a while! Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes, happy Lantern Rite! What brings you here, though? I thought you'd be in the harbor enjoying the Xiao Lanterns.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hmm, you're certainly not the type to visit Yujing Terrace for no reason. Is there something I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What, we're not allowed to just drop in on our friends during the festive season?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I was only teasing. You're welcome to visit us anytime you wish. Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and about all the moon business you were just talking about... We have something to show you. Here, take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Whoa, something really did take a chunk out of the moon!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Someone managed to capture a picture of it? Is this... Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer, then?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Even though we confirmed this event took place, I still can't quite believe what I'm seeing... Where did you get this picture?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From Xiangling! She found it when she was cleaning up after that customer caused a scene. She thinks they must've dropped it.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Wait, is this... Chiwang Terrace?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: No, no, it's just... Where I'm from, it's said that Chiwang Terrace was where the ancient people of Chenyu Vale communicated with the heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: And in this picture, the moon happens to be right above Chiwang Terrace. I was just surprised, that's all... It's probably just a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: That's interesting because... the ancient people of Chenyu Vale migrated there from the Chasm area.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Chasm? So that place is involved too?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: According to our investigation, that customer you just mentioned, Lu Xiangxiang... Her father and grandfather are merchants in Liyue Harbor, and her mother and grandmother grow tea in Qiaoying Village.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: A few days ago, she left her home in Qiaoying Village to join a civilian archaeological team funded by Huishan Hall, and ended up excavating some artifacts in the Chasm area.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: These artifacts were then entrusted to Xigu Antiques, and are set to be featured in an upcoming exhibition. Then, of course, the incident at Wanmin Restaurant occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: We suspect something happened during the excavation that left her with quite the shock.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: And now, it seems like she also went to Chiwang Terrace and took that picture of the moon disappearing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Chasm... Chiwang Terrace... Things are getting pretty complicated!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's Lu Xiangxiang doing now?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: She's not in a good mental state, so we took her to Bubu Pharmacy to get some help.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Why don't you come with me to check up on her? At this point, you seem invested in this case too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Gladly.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Then let's head there now.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: #Ah, Lady Yuheng. Oh, and {NICKNAME} and Paimon are here as well.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: What a pleasant surprise. Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I hope we're not interrupting, Dr. Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Not at all. I assume you're here to see the patient? Unless it's urgent, however, it would be best not to disturb her rest.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is her condition that bad?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It's quite unstable. She's even more agitated than when she first arrived, and she refused to cooperate when we tried to check her over.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I had no choice but to prescribe a calming draught and have her rest for two days.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: So she's getting worse? That isn't the news I was hoping for...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It's just a precaution. Based on an earlier conversation with her, it seemed more like a fixation than anything else. She hasn't lost her mind.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: That's right. When we asked about it, she kept insisting she was going to be famous far and wide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it might not be "far and wide," but she's certainly made a name for herself around Yujing Terrace... Even some of the Qixing know who she is!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you ever seen something like this, Baizhu?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Not often, that's for certain. From my initial assessment, the patient appears to have experienced some sort of shock, and whatever it was seems to still be haunting her.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: But, what could have caused such a thing...? The relics from The Chasm? Or the moon above Chiwang Terrace that night?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Come back in two days, and you might just have your answer.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I suppose that's all we can do for now. We'll take our leave then, Dr. Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Of course. If you need anything else, don't hesitate to stop by.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of those relics from The Chasm, aren't they being featured in an exhibition tonight?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That's right. Are you planning to attend?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We wanted to have a talk with Zhongli anyway, and now Paimon's even more curious about these relics!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to tag along?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Haha, I would, except every item in the exhibition had to be registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs, so I'm afraid it's been spoiled for me. I reviewed them all myself.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: There are some rather peculiar artifacts, that's for certain. We're still working on decoding the ancient text that appears on them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, the word "jade" appears a whole bunch, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Huh? How did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xingqiu told us! He said there were some ancient poems on them too.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: He's quite well-informed, isn't he? Well, he's right. We believe they're direct references to the ancient nation of Lang-Gan.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: As for the other text... Instead of regular poetry, it seems to be more like ceremonial language used to worship the moon and the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The moon and the gods...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Well, looks like it's almost time for the exhibition. You two should head over.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: There's an usher at the harbor who will lead you to the venue.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do we need an invitation?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Not at all. The exhibition is free to the public. The people of Liyue have a great respect for our history and are eager to learn from it.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Plus, the exhibition is being organized by Linlang, the owner of Xigu Antiques.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: As far as I know, it's been a long-time goal of hers to hold a cultural exhibition of this scale, where people can learn all sorts of information about the past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we're in for a real treat tonight, then!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes, have a great time. There's still more artifact-decoding work I need to finish, so we'll have to part ways here.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: After seeing the picture you brought, there's a few ideas I'd like to follow up on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're hard at work even during festival season, huh... You haven't changed one bit, Keqing.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I'm simply fulfilling the responsibilities of my position, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Alright, I should get going. See you later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess we should head over to the harbor and find that usher!

dialogues.speaker: Manmu
dialogues.text: Ah, here for the exhibition? I can take you aboard.

response.speaker: Manmu
response.text: After you.

response.speaker: Manmu
response.text: Of course. I'll be here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look at all the antiques on this ship! It's almost too much to take in!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Keep an eye out for Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Greetings. I trust you've been well since last we met.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha, speak of the devil! You're right where Hu Tao said you'd be!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Ah, so Director Hu gave me away, did she...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't act like you're up to some super secret business. We know you just do whatever you feel like...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: #Yo, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! What's up!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: It's been a while, you two! Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Beidou! Yun Jin! It's great to see you! You're here for the exhibition too?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Yes! When I heard these artifacts were from ancient times, I just knew I had to come learn more about them. I mean, what a discovery, right?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Yeah, Ningguang pretty much said the same thing. She thought coming here might help "culture" me up, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: But as you know, I'm more of a fists and punches type of person. I doubt one exhibition is gonna change that, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: You're too modest, Captain. You're the leader of the Crux Fleet. That takes far more skill than just fists and punches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, at the end of the day, you still decided to come, even though you didn't have to listen to Ningguang.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Heh, well she's the Tianquan. If she can't even get an average ship captain like me to do her bidding, how's that gonna look?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure know how to think from her perspective, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Haha, I guess I do. Anyway, how's everyone enjoying the exhibition?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I heard that if you see something you like, you can negotiate the price with the owner and take it home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so we can buy this stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. Although Xigu Antiques is hosting this exhibition, many of the items come from private collectors. As long as both parties reach an agreement, you can make an offer of Mora or an equivalent trade.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Well, shall we continue our conversation as we look around?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go! Paimon's super curious about all this stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look at this painting! There's a huge toad on it! Could it be...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Huh, this material is quite unusual — it doesn't look like paper. More like silk or some other kind of fabric.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Yeah, I was thinking the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Heh, well-spotted. This is a painting of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer, made primarily with mulberry silk. Such craftsmanship is rarely seen in modern-day Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer! Paimon knew it! That toad made it super obvious.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: What's that? A new dish at Wanmin Restaurant?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, hehehe... It's a kind of lunar eclipse! You heard about how the moon disappeared recently, right?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... You're saying a toad did that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what the legend says!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hah, so nothing to do with food, then. Noted.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: And the figure next to the toad... Is that the White Horse Adeptus? From the stories I've heard, her palace lies on the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: That would seem to be a logical assumption.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was this excavated from The Chasm?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No. In fact, this item was discovered in Chenyu Vale, and many years ago at that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so it's from Chenyu Vale?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Actually, that's not quite right. You see, this painting is primarily comprised of mineral-based pigments such as cinnabar and azurite, which are usually found within stratified rock.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This suggests its place of origin may very well have been The Chasm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You could have just started with that!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: You're as knowledgeable as ever, Mr. Zhongli. I had only ever heard the legend of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer, but now seeing it depicted in this painting, I wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: If I purchased it, perhaps it could serve as inspiration for a new opera. Though I'm not quite sure who the painting belongs to right now...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A splendid idea, Ms. Yun. Perhaps, in lieu of Mora, you could offer the lyrics to said opera as recompense?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: The lyrics? But, to whom...?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Why, to me of course. I am the owner of this painting, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you're one of the private collectors at the exhibition? No wonder you knew so much about the painting...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: But... lyrics in exchange for a precious antique? My work could never possibly be of equal value.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Mm, I don't know about that. I'm not much of a scholar, but even I know your operas are in a league of their own.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: An astute observation, Captain Beidou. In my possession, this painting is nothing but a lifeless artifact.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: In your hands, however, it could be transformed into a new piece of art entirely. Quite the worthy exchange, no?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: But I'm not sure when I'll be able to finish writing it. It certainly won't be ready this year...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Allow me to be equally forthright, Ms. Yun — this silk painting is merely a copy I made of the original work. There is no need for such concern over its value.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So it's a fake!?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I had no idea you were such a skilled artist, Mr. Zhongli. I pride myself on having some knowledge of antiques, but I didn't notice anything that would point to it being a replica.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha! You never cease to amaze me, Mr. Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You flatter me. All that said, Ms. Yun, you must accept. Truly, I insist.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph... He's gone from handing out fake Mora to fake paintings now, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shh...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Your kindness is impossible to refuse, Mr. Zhongli. Rest assured, I'll be sure to return the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I shall look forward to it.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Man, that was quite the find. Heh, I should buy something too, if only so I can show it off to Ningguang.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, let's keep going and see what we can find!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Wow, this bronze war chariot is really something.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Hmm, it must have quite the story behind it. I've never seen anything like it before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know what this is, Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Ah, I heard from Miss Linlang that a carriage made of celadon jade was unearthed in The Chasm.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A copper canopy, a body adorned with flowing clouds and geometric patterns... Yes, this must be the one. A precious piece indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: This thing's gotta be thousands of years old, right? Crazy to think people back then were capable of such intricate metalwork.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Too often, we view the past and future through the lens of the present. Objects that fascinated us as children seem crude later in life, and that's only after a few decades or so of separation.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: If one were to stretch time across hundreds or thousands of years... one might discover that time is not always a force that pushes things forward.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: It would seem the people of that era managed to create a remarkable civilization in their own right.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Heh, makes me wanna get my hands on this even more. Ningguang's gonna be so jealous, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Ah, has this war chariot caught your eye, Captain Beidou?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Oh, you must be Linlang from Xigu Antiques. Nice to meet you! This exhibition has been amazing so far.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Well, that's all thanks to supportive patrons like you, and Mr. Zhongli of course.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: As for this war chariot, it was discovered by an archaeological team sponsored by Huishan Hall. The price comes in at 90 million Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—How much!?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Ninety million? Ha! Looks like my eyes were a bit too big for my wallet...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hmm... Quite a bargain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A bargain!? 90 million Mora could feed Paimon for like... a thousand years!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Heh, and if you actually went on an eating spree that long, perhaps you'd be considered an antique worth that kind of Mora too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What, 90 million? Nuh-uh, Paimon's worth way more than that!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well if Mr. Zhongli thinks it's a good deal, I'm sure it's worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Beidou's putting way too much faith in Zhongli. What if he's only here to drive up sales!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shh.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I'll take the chariot, Miss Linlang. Someone will come by with the payment.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Quite the discerning eye you have, Captain. After the exhibition ends, I'll have someone deliver it to The Alcor.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Actually, could you send it straight to Yujing Terrace? I'd like for the Tianquan to see the proof of my "discerning eye" for herself.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Hehe, understood.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Great, Yun Jin and I both found something. What about you three? Wanna keep perusing?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Don't worry about the Mora — it's all on me. Nobody's going home empty-handed tonight!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I appreciate your kindness, Captain, but I'm afraid I have some private matters to discuss with Miss Linlang.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: In that case, don't let us keep you, Mr. Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Right this way.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, perhaps you would like to accompany me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What, so you can show us another "bargain" antique that's so far out of our price range it's not even funny?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Other people are always demanding Mr. Zhongli's time, but it's quite rare for him to extend an invitation himself. I wouldn't pass up this opportunity if I were you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Yeah! Just don't forget to come aboard The Alcor for a drink later.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should at least check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, guess you're right. Taking a quick look isn't gonna cost us anything. Let's go!

talks.objective: Accompany Zhongli to browse further at the exhibition

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: These are all the jade pieces that were found, Mr. Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so many styles! What kind are these?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: These are a type of ceremonial jade. You're familiar with Chenyu Vale's Rainjade Rite, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! So these pieces are all used in the Rainjade ceremony?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Well, you may not know, Paimon, but before the "Rainjade Rite" came into practice, Chenyu Vale was known for a different ceremonial tradition that also involved jade.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Bi is used to honor Heaven, the Cong to honor Earth, the Gui to honor the East, the Zhang to honor the South, the Hu to honor the West, and the Huang to honor the North. These form the Six Ritual Jades.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It's unfortunate, however, that Miss Linlang's set is missing both the Gui and Hu pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: I know. These jade artifacts are from such an ancient time, it's proved difficult to track them down, even for our establishment.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No matter. You happen to have precisely the piece I was looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Huh? This broken jade token? I didn't expect this to catch your eye, Mr. Zhongli. It isn't one of the Six Ritual Jades.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: An effect belonging to an old acquaintance of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: An old acquaintance? One of your collector friends, Mr. Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #Heh, you could say that. {NICKNAME}, take a closer look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, it doesn't look all that special to Paimon. Just seems like a broken artifact.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a crescent moon.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. It's been thousands of years since the moon has appeared in such a form.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: So, in the past, the moon wasn't always full? Then... Could this missing chunk be from when Zhanzhu devoured part of the moon?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Mmm... It's worth looking into.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Your insight is invaluable, Mr. Zhongli. I had no idea how special this piece was.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Since it has caught your interest, allow Xigu Antiques to cover the cost.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: That is far too generous, Miss Linlang.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Not at all. I've always wanted to give people a chance to appreciate these snapshots of history, so holding an exhibition like this has been a lifetime wish of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: And it never would have been possible without your help, Mr. Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I merely put in a good word with a few acquaintances of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: And it had a profound impact. Without your recommendation, I doubt half of these collectors would have come to the exhibition. So, on both a personal and professional level, I owe you my thanks, Mr. Zhongli.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Zhongli actually did something useful for once...

talks.objective: Accompany Zhongli to browse further at the exhibition

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What just happened? How did I get here...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That light ahead looks like it could be an exit... I should check it out.)

talks.objective: Approach the distant ball of light
Approach the distant ball of light

dialogues.text: Eleven... Thirteen... Seventeen...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who said that?
Nineteen... Twenty-three... Twenty-nine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thirty-one?
You also enjoy counting in such a fashion, lost child?
Hm, the same loneliness as them... It seems to exist in your heart as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?
Me...? I'm sorry, I... don't remember.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What is this place?
...The shadow of the moon? Or... a dream of time?
I'm sorry, no one has asked me such things before. I've been here for so long, there is much I have forgotten...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you bring me here?
I know nothing of your arrival. All I know is the longing in people's hearts...
Yet... I sense the moonlight's guidance within you, child. Perhaps that is what brought you here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The moonlight's guidance... Does she mean... Columbina?)
You seem confused. Perhaps I can help in some way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do I get out of here?
The path home is... that direction. I believe someone told me that before...
...But I was never able to reach the end.
You should take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about we go together?
No need. It would seem... my time has already run out.
Farewell. May the moonlight ever shine upon you.

talks.objective: Accompany Zhongli to browse further at the exhibition

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Zhongli actually did something useful for once...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm... back?)

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #Your complexion looks rather ashen, {NICKNAME}. Are you feeling alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! What's wrong? Does your stomach hurt?

choices.text: I just met the strangest person...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What are you talking about? You were right here the whole time...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah... I see...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #I'm afraid we must take our leave, Miss Linlang. My friend has taken ill, and I must escort {M#him}{F#her} to get some rest.

response.speaker: Linlang
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, please come with me.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah, yes, regarding the payment for the jade token — charge the expense to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, if you would.

choices.text: I was just in the strangest place...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...Ahhchoo!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Guess someone's thinking of me, hehe. Huh, but this late at night?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Must be that consultant of yours! I bet he's out there spending all your Mora at the exhibition.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aiya, he'd be the perfect employee if he just knew how to rein in the spending. But never mind him, let's focus on the moon! We gotta see if it gets eaten tonight!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I don't think it's going to happen. We've been out here all night, and the moon's the same as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It is quite late, and Chongyun's getting tired.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: How about we head back? We can come back another time.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Head back? Already?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Actually, I do have a new dish I'm testing out tomorrow, and as part of my New Year's resolution, I'm trying not to oversleep.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. Guess it just wasn't meant to be. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: When the sun's out, bathe in sunlight. When the moon's out, bathe in moonlight~

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, weren't we going to rest? Why did you bring us here?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #Because I imagine {NICKNAME} would like to know what just happened to {M#him}{F#her}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh right. Ugh, Paimon's confused though. She could've sworn you were there the whole time!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain your mysterious encounter in that strange space.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—How is that possible?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #It sounds like {M#his}{F#her} spirit formed an inexplicable connection with the being in that space.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was it the White Horse Adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Ah, you suspected from the beginning, didn't you? Indeed, the being you met is the fabled White Horse Adeptus, and the original owner of this jade token. Her name is Zibai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, does that mean... she's inside this token!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No, she does not reside within this token, but rather... within the moon's shadow. This token is merely a medium.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The moon's shadow? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Word has it, you accomplished quite the feat in Nod-Krai. You and your friend... brought the Frost Moon back to Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Tell me, did you ever wonder about the other moon, the one that hung in its place for thousands of years?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We never really thought about it, but... it must have been a fake, right? A fake moon!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed, it was false — its true nature nothing but a projection of the moon. It also happens to be the prison that confines Zibai to this day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, the White Horse Adeptus is trapped inside that projection!? Then, we need to rescue her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... the moon in the sky right now is the real one, right? Where did the fake moon go, and why can't Paimon see it?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: With the return of the true moon, the shadow naturally lost its place in the heavens. Now, it is disintegrating bit by bit. It's a process that comes and goes.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: When it occurs, it looks like the moon is being obscured by a black shadow. But when it stops, the shadow disappears and becomes invisible to the eye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So you're saying there's an invisible fake moon blocking the real moon, right now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, the recent lunar eclipse... It was the fake moon, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, this is not what Paimon was expecting!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You said it's disintegrating. When will there be nothing left?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: My hypothesis is that people's wishes could be what trigger the periods of disintegration. After all, when you experienced that episode just now, it was precisely when Miss Linlang spoke of her own wish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is that because the White Horse Adeptus answers people's wishes? The legend must be true, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that means the more wishes we make, the faster the fake moon will disintegrate, right? Then it won't be long before the White Horse Adeptus is free!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Quite the contrary. After countless years trapped inside, the two have merged into one. When the moon's shadow is gone, Zibai will cease to exist in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... So, by bringing the moon back, we actually... hurt the White Horse Adeptus!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Do not burden yourself with such thoughts. Because of your actions, a promising opportunity has presented itself to us — let us not forget, what is crumbling is also precisely that which imprisons her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So there's still a way to fix this?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Yes, and that is why I invited you here tonight. Your connection to that broken jade token confirms that you can do what I envision.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: However, while I had hoped to receive your assistance, this matter could have significant ramifications...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I must admit a certain... reluctance to implicate you in more of Teyvat's secrets. Often, the deeper one's knowledge of such matters, the harder it becomes to extricate oneself from them.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You are someone who once traveled through the boundless sea of stars. I cannot help but wonder... Perhaps it is wrong for your fate to become too entangled with the fate of any one world...

choices.text: I already know a bunch of secrets.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hmm... Such is your conviction, then. Since journeying beyond Liyue, you have had ample time to reflect on these matters, it would seem.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes. So, tell me what I need to do.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Very well. The first secret I must reveal is that Zibai has long since passed away. The being within the shadowmoon is merely one of the Three Deadly Selves she severed before her death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, the White Horse Adeptus is dead!? Weren't you supposed to tell us how to fix this? Now, it just seems even more impossible...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Please remain calm, Paimon, and allow me to explain.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The Three Deadly Selves is a practice used by those engaged in spiritual cultivation. The intent is to sever the three vice-laden mortal selves to reveal one's true, pure self beneath. However, Zibai's Three Selves are more complicated in nature.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Because in the moment before her death, someone preserved the shattered essence of her soul, and placed the fragments within her Three Deadly Selves.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: If we retrieve the three fragments of her soul, there is a chance we can restore her presence in the mortal realm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that means... we can bring her back to life!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yes, provided we retrieve the fragments of her soul's essence from the Three Deadly Selves.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm guessing I just met one of them.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed. The being you encountered was Zibai's First Deadly Self, Ziju. After Zibai's death, she ascended to the heavens and became one with the shadowmoon.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The essence that resides within her is a Heavenly Soul, also known as Taiguang. Thus, this Self is the closest to Zibai's true nature.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That said, because she is trapped within the shadowmoon, we have no choice but to seek out the other two soul essences first. Then, we can unite them as one.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, so... where are the other two?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Her Second Deadly Self is called Zizhi. After Zibai's death, she fell into a slumber deep beneath the earth in what is now known as The Chasm.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The essence within her is the Earth Soul, also known as Shuangling. She is the Self that inherited most of Zibai's memories and wisdom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Chasm... So, do we have to go there to find her?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That won't be necessary. I sensed her presence on the jade carriage from earlier, the one at the exhibition.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's possible the return of the Frost Moon awakened her, and she emerged from the Chasm alongside that batch of ancient artifacts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, that must be why you agreed to help with the exhibition... To investigate the artifacts!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed. So in truth, Miss Linlang was the one who helped me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about the last Deadly Self?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The Third Deadly Self is Zijiao. The essence within her is the Human Soul — also known as Youjing, Zibai's shade. Thus, she is the most free-spirited among the three.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: She lent me her aid during the Archon War a thousand years ago. But later, as her powers waned, she retreated into the mountains.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I imagine finding Zijiao should prove the most troublesome, so I shall take it upon myself to track her down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we need to find the Second Deadly Self, right? But where do we even start?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Locating her should not prove difficult. In life, Zibai was fond of mortals, and as the Self who inherited most of her memories and wisdom, Ziju should be the same.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's possible she has possessed someone and is meandering the bustling streets of Liyue Harbor as we speak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Possessed someone? Wait... Are you thinking what Paimon's thinking, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The customer who caused a scene at Wanmin Restaurant.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: What if she raided a tomb and dug up some super special relic, then got herself haunted by an ancient ghost!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Lu Xiangxiang!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It seems you have a lead in mind already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She'd still be at Bubu Pharmacy! She was super agitated when she first got there, so Baizhu gave her some calming medicine and told us to come back in two days.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you think it could be her, Zhongli?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's quite possible. The Deadly Selves are impure beings that can easily influence mortal minds...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's start our investigation there in two days.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: A sound plan. Well, I should get started on my own investigation, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wha— You're leaving already?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I must. Zijiao went into hiding after the Archon War. If I am to have any success tracking her down — and there is no guarantee — I should start sooner rather than later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But there's still so much you haven't told us... Like who the White Horse Adeptus actually is, and how she died in the first place...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not to mention who it was that preserved the fragments of her soul...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Should our endeavor prove successful, then naturally, those answers will follow. If not, speaking of them would be rather meaningless.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The one who preserved her soul's essence... Was it you?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...It would seem that this is a question you are unwilling to set aside. Very well, I shall tell you.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...It was the avatar of Time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Istaroth!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah, so you know of her existence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Ruler of Time saved her soul...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed. Preserving what remained of Zibai's soul in the moment before her death... Only the power of time could be capable of such a thing.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: However, there is no telling what effect it has had on the Three Deadly Selves. In other words, you must exercise caution when seeking out Zizhi.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How much time do we have?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: On the night of Lantern Rite, countless Xiao Lanterns — and the wishes written upon them — will be released into the sky. I estimate that this event will trigger the shadowmoon's collapse.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: When that happens, the cage that confines the First Deadly Self will open. That is our moment to act, but also the moment where all could be lost.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: For if we fail to retrieve the other two soul fragments in time, Zibai's resurrection is hopeless.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: As I mentioned before, the answers to your remaining question should come in time, providing our efforts bear fruit.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Let us hope that all proceeds smoothly in the days to come.

choices.text: I'm already deeply connected to Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: #Morning, split bamboo, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Oh no, I got it wrong again.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: May the White Horse Adeptus bless us and watch over our business.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: If you're looking to talk to Lu Xiangxiang, you should come back in two days.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Mr. Zhongli is having tea at Third-Round Knockout. Good luck!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hmm... Now that I see this picture, it looks less like a piece of the moon was eaten, and more like something is obscuring it...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: But what sort of thing could block out the moon?

dialogues.speaker: Lin Xing
dialogues.text: The patient is resting. No disturbances, please.

dialogues.speaker: Wu Wu
dialogues.text: The patient is resting. No disturbances, please.
Three... Five... Seven...
